`AbstractRouteCollection` decides the outcome. After a miss it probes the other verbs (`checkForAlternateVerbs`). If any verb matches, `getRouteForMethods` returns a synthesized 200 with an `Allow` header for OPTIONS, or throws `MethodNotAllowedHttpException` (405) for other verbs. If no verb matches, it throws `NotFoundHttpException` (404). `CompiledRouteCollection::match` handles the compiled fast path and falls back to this logic on a miss, and `Router.php` defines the verb list (including OPTIONS) and the `options()` registration.

The core logic is in `AbstractRouteCollection`: when no route matches, `checkForAlternateVerbs()` tests the other verbs. If any match, it throws a 405 (`MethodNotAllowedHttpException`) with the allowed methods, and for OPTIONS it returns a 200 response with an `Allow` header instead. If none match, it throws a 404 (`NotFoundHttpException`).

`Repository::flexible()` stores the value plus a "created" timestamp, returns the cached value immediately, and when it is past its fresh window it defers a locked rebuild (`defer()`) that writes a new value only if the created timestamp is unchanged, so the value keeps being served until the rebuild finishes. `DeferredCallback` is the class that runs that work after the response is sent, and `functions.php` and `helpers.php` provide the global `defer()` helper that creates it.
